dedupe_keys.name: alberta wells dataset oil and gas wells from satellite imagery

description: The Alberta Wells Dataset is a large benchmark for finding oil and gas wells, including abandoned ones, in satellite imagery. It was published on Zenodo in September 2024 by Pratinav Seth, Michelle Lin, Brefo Dwamena Yaw, Jade Boutot, Mary Kang and David Rolnick, motivated by the millions of abandoned wells that leak methane and contaminate groundwater, many at unknown locations. It pairs medium-resolution multispectral imagery from Planet Labs with more than 213,000 abandoned, suspended and active wells in Alberta taken from the Alberta Energy Regulator and checked by experts, and it reports baseline detection and segmentation results. Coverage is Alberta, Canada. The data are split training, validation and test archives of several gigabytes each, downloadable from Zenodo at no cost under CC BY-NC 4.0 for academic, non-commercial use, with credit to the authors, Planet Labs and the Alberta Energy Regulator. Caveats: raw imagery cannot be shared publicly under the Planet licence, and the archives are very large. Simulation uses are mapping unrecorded wells for exposure and environmental risk studies and training asset detection models. Related records: data-ogim-oil-gas-infrastructure-mapping maps oil and gas facilities worldwide.
